title: Salary On-Costs Calculator Australia: Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top
description: Use our salary on-costs calculator Australia to convert hourly rates to annual pay, including casual loading and super. Based on Fair Work and ATO data.
salarySummary: Based on a 38‑hour week, the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour gives an annual salary of $52,254.80 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual salary calculation?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. For example, the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour for casual employees. When using a salary on-costs calculator Australia, you should enter the base rate (without loading) and then apply the 25% loading separately. Our calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the annual salary figure or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% (from 1 July 2026) and is not deducted from your salary. When you use a salary on-costs calculator Australia, the annual salary shown is your gross pay before super. The estimated super amount is added separately and is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year.

faqs.q: What tax rates apply to my annual salary in 2026–27?
faqs.a: For Australian residents in 2026–27, the tax‑free threshold is $18,200. Income from $18,201 to $45,000 is taxed at 15%, then 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy of 2% applies to most taxpayers. Our salary on-costs calculator Australia uses these rates and assumes you claim the tax‑free threshold. Note that HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary sacrifice are not included.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Salary with a Salary On-Costs Calculator Australia

When you’re negotiating a job offer or comparing hourly rates, it’s essential to see the full picture. A **salary on-costs calculator Australia** helps you convert an hourly rate into annual pay, while also accounting for casual loading, superannuation, and tax. This guide explains the key components so you can use our calculator with confidence.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

Annual gross pay is calculated by multiplying your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. Our calculator assumes a standard full‑time week of **38 hours**, as defined by the Fair Work Act. For example:

- $26.44 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = **$52,254.80 per year**

This is the national minimum wage from 1 July 2026, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you work different hours, you can adjust the weekly hours in the calculator.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

Casual employees are entitled to a **25% loading** on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. The loading is applied to the base rate, not to a rate that already includes loading. Our calculator has a checkbox to add the 25% loading automatically.

For the minimum wage, the casual rate becomes:
- $26.44 × 1.25 = **$33.05 per hour**

This matches the casual rate published by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Always use the base rate first, then add loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top of Your Salary

Employers must pay super guarantee contributions of **12%** (from 1 July 2026) on your ordinary earnings. This is paid **on top** of your salary, not deducted from it. The maximum earnings subject to super is $270,830 per year (the maximum contribution base).

When using a salary on-costs calculator Australia, the annual salary shown is your gross pay. The estimated super amount is calculated separately. For example, on a $52,254.80 salary, the super contribution would be:
- $52,254.80 × 12% = **$6,270.58** (if under the cap)

### Tax Withholding and Medicare Levy

The Australian Taxation Office provides a tax withheld calculator for employers. Our calculator uses the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). The calculator assumes you claim the tax‑free threshold. If you have a HELP debt or Medicare levy surcharge, these are not included.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Most Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the minimum wage:
- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: **$2,009.80**

Our calculator shows both weekly and fortnightly figures to help with budgeting.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The national minimum wage applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most industries have **award rates** that are higher. You can check the correct rate for your job using the pay guides from the Fair Work Ombudsman. Our calculator allows you to enter any hourly rate, so you can use the award rate that applies to you.

### What the Calculator Does Not Include

This salary on-costs calculator Australia provides an estimate only. It assumes:
- The same rate every week (no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances)
- No salary sacrifice arrangements
- No HELP or other loan repayments
- No Medicare levy surcharge

For a precise determination of your pay and tax, consult your employer or a registered tax agent.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

To track your hours and pay, try our [timesheet](/). For more detailed pay guides, visit the [pay guides](/blog) page. You can also explore [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) information and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimates.

### Summary

A salary on-costs calculator Australia helps you see the full cost of employment. Remember:
- Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52
- Casual loading adds 25% to the base rate
- Super is 12% paid on top, capped at $270,830
- Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates plus Medicare

Use our calculator to compare job offers, plan your budget, and understand your entitlements.
